newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two U.S. youths die in car crash on Japan's Okinawa.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. youths die in car crash on Japan's Okinawa.

text.p: Two U.S. youths died in a car accident on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa after the car struck a lamp pole, police said on Sunday.

Anthony Sacco, 20, and Arron Armel, 17, died when the car, driven by 17-year-old Johann Feller, skidded on a wet road at high speed early on Sunday morning and hit a street lamp on a coastal road in central Okinawa, police said.
Feller, who did not have a driver's licence, and a third passenger, Richard Angubat, 18, were seriously injured and are in hospital, police said.
The two deceased were dependents of civilians employed by U.S. armed forces on the island.
About half of the 47,000 U.S. forces stationed in Japan are based on Okinawa, 1,600 km (1,000 miles) southwest of Tokyo, along with a large population of civilian employees and their dependents.
Okinawans have protested against the large concentration of bases on the small subtropical island and the noise, crime and accidents associated with the U.S. troops.
